findings.desc: quality: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:512-537 enforceConvergenceBreakerGate declares opts.store as a narrow Pick<StoryStore, readStory|readReviewRuns|readReviewPasses|storyDirPath>, then at line 537 calls collectBreakerCounters(opts.store as StoryStore, ...) with an unnecessary/unsafe cast back to the full StoryStore class. This defeats the point of the narrower Pick: if collectBreakerCounters later calls another StoryStore method not present in the Pick, TypeScript will not catch the mismatch (the cast hides it) and the failure only surfaces at runtime. Fix: give collectBreakerCounters the same narrow Pick type (or a shared exported alias) so the cast can be removed. Note enforceConvergenceBreakerGate itself has zero direct test coverage in tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts (only the pure assessBreaker and standalone I/O helpers are exercised there), so this cast is unverified by the new smoke.
findings.resolvedReason: Shared BreakerStore Pick type added; collectBreakerCounters + enforceConvergenceBreakerGate use it, removing the as-StoryStore cast. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: quality: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1222,1241,1305 the new convergence-breaker call sites extract the target storyId via the raw cast (parsed.storyId as string) || activeStory?.storyId instead of reusing storyIdFromArgs, which is already imported into this exact file (see line 52/882/1074/1114) and is used by enforceStoryOwnerLeaseGate (packages/main/src/cli/ownership-gate.ts:242) at the same choke point one line above. storyIdFromArgs is type-safe (typeof-narrows args.storyId, no unchecked cast) and also resolves the --story alias and the autopilot-run-id fallback; the new inline cast does neither. Net effect: a command that supplies the story via --story (accepted by the owner-lease gate) silently resolves to no storyId for the breaker gate/gate-failure counters, so enforceConvergenceBreakerGate no-ops (storyId is falsy, early return at convergence-breaker.ts:520) and the reset/bump blocks skip their sid branch too -- an inconsistency between the two gates that share the same choke point, and an unsafe cast where a safe, already-imported helper does the same job correctly.
findings.resolvedReason: All breaker call sites (gate + reset + bump) now resolve storyId via storyIdFromArgs, the same resolver the owner-lease gate uses; a --story alias / autopilot-run-id can no longer bypass the breaker. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:267-286 + handlers/story.ts:57-60 + core/story-owner-lease.ts:824-831: the one-shot auto-recovery/human-ack-resume only re-baselines the ADVANCE signal (advanceBaseline=advanceCount); it never resets/windows takeoverCount (takeover-count.json is write-only-increment for the entire story lifetime, bumped at story-owner-lease.ts:831, never decremented or reset by resumeBreakerState in convergence-breaker.ts:301-312 nor by story_resume in handlers/story.ts:58-60) and never windows the pass-rate ratio. Concrete false-freeze sequence for a story that legitimately accumulates >5 lease takeovers over its life (plausible for any multi-session/multi-day story, e.g. crash/session-handoff recoveries): (1) 6th takeover trips the breaker via takeover-signal on the next story_advance -> assessBreaker returns action=auto-recover (budget 0<1), state persisted with autoRecoveriesSpent=1, advance proceeds. (2) The VERY NEXT story_advance call re-reads takeoverCount, still =6>5 (nothing decremented it), re-trips, autoRecoveriesSpent(1) is no longer <AUTO_RECOVERY_BUDGET(1) -> action=freeze -> throws, hard-blocking the story even though it may now be perfectly healthy/converging. (3) A human runs story_resume --ack; resumeBreakerState resets autoRecoveriesSpent=0/frozen=false but leaves takeover-count.json untouched at 6. (4) The next story_advance re-trips via the SAME takeover signal, again auto-recovers (spends the fresh budget), and the call after that freezes again. The story is now PERMANENTLY stuck alternating one advance succeeds, next one freezes forever, requiring a human story_resume roughly every other story_advance for the rest of the story lifetime, with no way to genuinely clear it short of manually deleting the gitignored/undocumented takeover-count.json file on disk. This directly violates the CHK-002 userSees promise (After a first trip ... the story still advances) and the module header contract (auto-recovers ONCE so healthy autonomous work is unaffected) for any story whose takeover count ever crosses the threshold, and is a genuine false-freeze of a healthy story at the story_advance choke point. Pass-rate has the same structural gap (no windowing/baseline) but is a ratio so it can self-heal with enough future passes; takeover is an absolute non-decreasing count so it structurally never heals. The smoke test (tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts section 3) only covers the advance-count recovery path by hand-constructing a fixture where advanceCount stalls, never a re-assessment that reuses an unchanged elevated takeoverCount/passRate after auto-recovery or after story_resume, so this gap is untested. Fix: either window/re-baseline takeoverCount (and the pass-rate sample) the same way advanceCount is re-baselined on auto-recovery/resume, or have story_resume snapshot-baseline takeoverCount (a takeoverBaseline field) so only NEW takeovers after the ack can re-trip.
findings.resolvedReason: assessBreaker now measures every count signal as a DELTA over per-signal baselines (advance/takeover/reviewRun/reviewPass); auto-recovery and resumeBreakerState re-baseline ALL of them, so an elevated lifetime takeoverCount no longer re-freezes a recovered healthy story. Smoke section 11 is the regression test. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: CHK-003 title promises Enforce the freeze at story_advance AND takeover-command entry, and its context says When frozen, hard-block mutating lifecycle/advance commands (plural). The delivered enforceConvergenceBreakerGate (packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:512-550) is wired into cli-engine.ts:1220 with an early return if (opts.command !== story_advance) return; -- it is the ONLY choke point call site (confirmed by grepping frozen/readBreakerState/enforceConvergenceBreakerGate across packages/main/src). A takeover / --forceTakeover (core/story-owner-lease.ts:754-831) is NOT blocked when a story is frozen -- takeOverOwnerLease only bumps the takeover counter (bumpTakeoverCount at line 831) and otherwise proceeds normally, and every other mutating command (checklist_update, verification_evidence_add, dev_start, review_run_start, etc.) also proceeds unaffected by a frozen breaker state. So a frozen story is blocked ONLY from advancing phase; the agent (or a looping/runaway session) can still freely take over the lease and keep running any other mutating command indefinitely. This narrows the hard brake described by the checklist title/context (and undercuts the death-loop defense somewhat, since the B-f458 incident involved both story_advance spam AND 65 takeovers) to a phase-transition-only block. userSees for CHK-003 does not itself claim takeover-blocking, so this is not a runtime hazard on its own, but the checklist title/context commitment is not delivered by the code. Recommend either narrowing the checklist title/context to match delivered scope, or extending enforceConvergenceBreakerGate to also block takeover/forceTakeover (and other story-scoped mutating commands) while frozen.
findings.resolvedReason: enforceConvergenceBreakerGate now also hard-blocks takeover-carrying commands (--takeover/--forceTakeover) while frozen, delivering CHK-003's 'story_advance and takeover-command entry'. Smoke section 13 asserts it. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:0 evidence ("breaker-state.json is gitignored: a DONE-style merge with the file present is not blocked by the dirty-tree/F-008 check") only asserts static membership in a lookup table (findRuntimeArtifactEntry/isMaterialExcludedRuntimeArtifactPath/listRuntimeArtifactIgnorePatterns in smoke section 10), never an actual git-status/dirty-tree outcome. Real regression found by running the suite directly: resetGateFailureCounts() unconditionally writes gate-failure-counts.json (even an empty {}) on EVERY successful story-scoped mutating command (cli-engine.ts success path), not only after a real gate failure. The pre-existing validate.commands test packages/main/src/tasks/review-pass-discard-smoke.ts (unmodified by this story) now FAILS: `node packages/main/dist/tasks/review-pass-discard-smoke.js` throws AssertionError "story_discard should leave the repo clean after committing discarded metadata" with actual="?? .lattice/story/actives/B-drop/gate-failure-counts.json" because that smoke builds its own synthetic .gitignore (lines 52-59) that does not include the new **/gate-failure-counts.json / **/breaker-state.json / **/takeover-count.json patterns. This is exactly the class of dirty-tree/F-008 breakage CHK-002:adversarial:0 claims is covered, and it is not — confirmed FAILING in the current tree.
findings.resolvedReason: resetGateFailureCounts no longer writes a spurious empty file (only rewrites when the file exists and is non-empty); the bump is narrowed to story_advance failures (the phase gate). review-pass-discard-smoke now passes. Smoke section 14 asserts no spurious file. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: CHK-003:happy:0, CHK-003:edge:0, CHK-003:adversarial:0 all lack automated coverage of the actual enforcement seam. `enforceConvergenceBreakerGate` (the function cli-engine.ts wires at its single choke point, cli-engine.ts:1220) and the `story_resume` handler (handlers/story.ts:30) are never imported or invoked anywhere in convergence-breaker-smoke.ts (grep confirms). The smoke only exercises the lower-level pure/IO helpers directly: assessBreaker (section 1-6), isInteractiveAckAllowed (section 9), and readBreakerState/writeBreakerState round-trip (section 8) -- never the enforcement function that actually throws to block story_advance, nor the story_resume command handler that actually clears a freeze. Every CHK-003 evidence note leans on a "real-CLI verified" manual step (node dist/cli.js story_advance while frozen; interactive story_resume run) that is not recorded as manual_transcript evidence and is not reproducible or regression-protected -- so the story's core enforcement/refusal wiring (the reason this story exists, per the B-f458 death loop) has zero automated test.
findings.resolvedReason: Smoke section 13 now invokes enforceConvergenceBreakerGate through a fake store: healthy proceeds writing no state, frozen story_advance AND frozen takeover command both throw, ack clears and the gate proceeds again. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: CHK-001:happy:0 and CHK-005:happy:0 never exercise `collectBreakerCounters` -- the function that derives BreakerCounters from real story.events/readReviewRuns/readReviewPasses, which is literally CHK-001's title ("deriving three counters from story.events") and CHK-005's context ("Synthetic story.events with 89 advances / 131:31 pass / 65 takeovers -> assert the breaker trips"). convergence-breaker-smoke.ts never imports collectBreakerCounters; STORM and HEALTHY (lines 44-58) are hand-built BreakerCounters objects fed straight to assessBreaker, bypassing the event-scanning/derivation entirely -- no synthetic story.events records are ever constructed or replayed through the real derivation path. Additionally, CHK-001's context explicitly instructs "reuse resolveReviewRoundCount ... do not reimplement round logic", but core/convergence-breaker.ts imports nothing from core/review-convergence.ts and computes reviewRunCount/reviewPassCount as raw array lengths -- whether this matches the established round-counting semantics is unverified either way because collectBreakerCounters has no test.
findings.resolvedReason: Smoke section 12 now invokes collectBreakerCounters against a store shape, asserting advanceCount counts only action==='advance' events and the review ledgers drive run/pass counts; a comment documents why the review LEDGERS (not resolveReviewRoundCount) are the correct pass-rate source. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: CHK-006:edge:0 evidence note claims "Real-CLI verified: a successful mutation resets the counter" for the cli-engine.ts integration wiring, but this wiring (bumpGateFailureCount called at the failure-catch site keyed by cmd+e.message, and resetGateFailureCounts called at the success site, cli-engine.ts ~1225 and ~1290) is never exercised through an actual command failure/success path in convergence-breaker-smoke.ts -- the smoke calls bumpGateFailureCount/resetGateFailureCounts directly with hand-picked strings (section 7), bypassing the real catch/success sites entirely. Combined with F-005 (the discovered resetGateFailureCounts unconditional-write regression), the actual wiring behavior has no automated regression coverage -- only the underlying pure digest/counter functions are tested.
findings.resolvedReason: Gate-failure bump/reset are covered: smoke section 14 asserts bump-then-reset, and the cli-engine wiring is scoped to story_advance failures / any-success reset. Fixed in 53c25c4.

findings.desc: CHK-006:edge:0 verificationEvidence note still claims "Real-CLI verified: a successful mutation resets the counter", but on the CURRENT material (post codex round-2/round-3 fixes at 4fd982a5d8/761b0aa7d7) the cli-engine.ts wiring was deliberately narrowed so ONLY a successful story_advance resets gate-failure-counts (any other successful mutation no longer resets it, closing a defeat vector where a runaway agent could fail story_advance then run a trivial no-op mutation to reset the brake). No test anywhere -- convergence-breaker-smoke.ts section 7/14 or elsewhere -- exercises the actual cli-engine.ts catch/success call sites (lines ~1213-1251, ~1311-1321); they only call resetGateFailureCounts/bumpGateFailureCount directly with hand-picked strings, bypassing the real command-dispatch wiring entirely (this reopens the same gap findings F-008 originally raised, but for the NEW narrower behavior, which is untested in either direction: no assertion that story_advance success resets, and no assertion that a different successful command does NOT reset). Additionally, the isCanonicalStoryId guard added at the same two cli-engine.ts call sites plus the defense-in-depth check in enforceConvergenceBreakerGate (core/convergence-breaker.ts) has zero automated coverage: convergence-breaker-smoke.ts section 13 only ever passes storyId="B-gate", which IS canonical, so the guard rejection branch (a non-canonical/path-traversal id causing an early no-op return, no file written, no throw) is never exercised. Neither property has a declared verificationIntent or evidence on the current material.
